cars.label: NEAT 16
cars.title: NEAT 16: the proven recipe
cars.why:
The best NEAT recipe from the ladder (n05): 16 rays facing forward over ±120°, 2000-frame training episodes,
+1 fitness per frame a lap beats 1000 frames, population 100. Trained from scratch for 8 hours. (A first
run stopped at 3.5 h on a "no faster lap for 2 h" rule that a single lucky lap check fooled; it was continued to 8 h.)
cars.outcome: The steady one. Its fastest checkpoint came near the end of the 8 hours (generation 401) and finishes all five race tracks in 20.8 s on average, never touching the grass. Its quickest-to-finish checkpoint (13 min) is fragile: 3 of 5 race tracks.

cars.label: NEAT 32
cars.title: NEAT 32: twice the rays
cars.why:
Same as NEAT 16 but with 32 forward rays over the same ±120°: twice the detail ahead, but twice the inputs to evolve
and a slower simulation. Do more rays make a faster car, or only a slower-to-train one?
cars.outcome: More rays bought speed, slowly: its fastest checkpoint (6 h 10 min) laps in 19.2 s with a 16.7 s best, but misses one race track. Twice the inputs took about four times the training of NEAT 16 to reach its best laps.

cars.label: NEAT Smart
cars.title: NEAT Smart: every lesson at once
cars.why:
NEAT 16 plus three lessons from the ladder. (1) No compass inputs: cos/sin(heading) are useless on random tracks,
and in n00 evolution had already cut cos(heading) off. (2) Five tracks per generation instead of three, so a network
can't win by drawing easy tracks. (3) A stronger lap-time bonus (2 per frame) to push harder for speed.
cars.outcome: Two very different cars. After only 18 minutes it already finished all five race tracks (27 s laps), the best quickest-to-finish car. Its fastest checkpoint laps validation in 18.5 s and sets the quickest race laps of any car (16.4-16.6 s), but crashes out on 3 of 5 race tracks: the stronger speed bonus made it fast but fragile.
